tips: There are no rules about what you type. Describe what you want to do in your own words.
Can't remember a name? Type '@' followed by the first few letters.
Quirk Strain rises when you use your Quirk and falls on its own. From 60 your Drawback shows (50 for an Exceptional Quirk); from 80 it bites.
Every technique lists its cost: Strain for Quirk moves, Stamina for everything else.
Using a Quirk in public without a hero license is illegal. Self-defense and supervised training are the exceptions.
Heroes are judged on rescue as much as on fights. Getting people out counts.
Recovery Girl heals fast, but she spends your stamina to do it. Arrive exhausted and you will sleep it off.
Skills grow with use, and training counts. Try things your character is bad at.
Prices are in yen: an onigiri is about 150, a cafeteria lunch 500-800, a city train ride 200-400.
Part-time work pays about 1,100 yen an hour. Pros earn through agency contracts, rankings and merchandise.
Ask the Narrator answers from what your character could know or see.
Canon events will come, but they don't have to end the way they did on TV.
Classmates keep their own schedules: lectures, training, meals, part-time jobs. Look for them where they would be.
When Eraser Head looks at you, Emitter and Transformation Quirks switch off. Mutant features stay.
Villains are criminals with real consequences: the police, the heroes and Tartarus are real.
Support gear only gives its bonus while it is equipped.
If you don't know what to do, submit without an action and let the scene move.
People remember what you promised them. So do your rivals.
Your hero name can wait. The story will give you a moment to choose it.
Quirkless isn't helpless: analysis, gear and nerve open doors that power doesn't.
